cards.text: Ezekiel the priest is in the middle of a vision. The Spirit has carried him to Jerusalem, and God has just shown him idols and sun worship right at the temple of the LORD (Ezekiel 1:3; 8:3-16). Then God calls out in a loud voice: “Draw near, O executioners of the city, each with a weapon of destruction in hand.”

cards.question: Ezekiel sees men coming from the Upper Gate, which faces north. There are ___ of them, each with a weapon of slaughter in his hand.

cards.text: Walking with those six is one more man, clothed in linen. Six men are carrying weapons. This one has something else at his side.

cards.question: What does the man clothed in linen have at his side?

cards.text: All seven come in and stand beside the bronze altar. Then the glory of the God of Israel rises from above the cherubim and moves to the threshold of the temple.

cards.question: God calls the man in linen and sends him all through Jerusalem to put a mark on people's foreheads. Who gets the mark?

answers.text: Those who bring offerings to the altar
Those who live closest to the temple

cards.text: Every person who gets that mark is sighing and groaning over what's being done in that city. Then, as Ezekiel listens, God turns to the six and tells them to follow the man in linen through the city.

cards.question: God tells the six men to show pity to anyone who begs for it.

cards.text: God's orders cover everyone: old men, young men and maidens, women and children. But He gives the six one exception.

cards.question: Who are the six men told not to go near?
God tells the six men to begin at His ___.

cards.text: So they begin with the elders in front of the temple, and God says, “Defile the temple and fill the courts with the slain. Go forth!”
Out they go, killing throughout the city, and Ezekiel is left alone. I spent years alone in the back of a junk drawer, friend, and that was NOTHING like this.

cards.question: Ezekiel falls facedown and cries out to the Lord GOD. What does he ask?

answers.text: If He will destroy everyone left in Israel
Why He brought him to see Jerusalem
If he can go and warn the city first

cards.text: God answers him. The iniquity of the house of Israel and Judah is exceedingly great, the land is full of bloodshed, and the city is full of perversity.

cards.question: God says the people claim the LORD has ___ the land and doesn't see.
God says He won't look on the people with pity. What will He bring down upon their own heads?
The man clothed in linen comes back and reports that he has done what God commanded.

cards.text: Heavy batch today, friend. Take a breath. And if you need to go hug a cookie, I won't tell anybody. But this vision isn't over yet.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences. Only the opening card can go past two.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Ezekiel 9:4 says to mark the foreheads of "the men" sighing and groaning. The question changes this to "people's foreheads," and card 7 then says "Every person who gets that mark." The cards should use the text's word.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The first sentence only repeats the answer to card 6 (who gets the mark) and moves nothing forward. It also makes the card two beats: a recap and the order in 9:5.
This story card has four sentences. A story card can have only one or two.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Most story cards are flat retellings with almost none of Papa Dorin's voice. Cards 3, 5, 9 and 15 read like plain narration. Card 15 is close to a word-for-word reading of 9:9. A heavy passage can still carry his fatherly storyteller voice: his reactions, his disbelief, and lines that carry the moment.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.
